dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?

Hi, yes, hello. I'm calling about the water at the curb, it's, um, it's out in front of 477 Malbone Road, in the North End. It's been going on for days now and it's not even raining. There's no storm, nothing.
Okay, 477 Malbone. So water sitting at the curb, and it's dry out. Is it coming from the snow melt, or does it seem to be coming from somewhere else?

It's the melt, I think, from the piles, all the snow we had, it runs down and just sits there at the drain and, wait, hold on. [pause] No, Aarav, not now, I'm on the phone. Sorry. Practice in there, please. Sorry about that.
No worries at all. Is that a recorder I hear?

Yes, my daughter, she's got a recital thing at school and she is, uh, she's going over the same four notes. Anyway. The water pools right at the curb and then at night it freezes. Every morning it's a sheet of black ice, right where people walk to the bus. Somebody's going to go down. I've told, well, this isn't the first time I'm saying it, it keeps doing it every time it warms up and then freezes.
Right, and that's the stretch in front of your building, along the curb by the storm drain?

Yeah, by the drain, but the drain's not taking anything. And there's another thing. The manhole cover, right there, it looks off. Like it's sitting an inch higher, or lower, I can't tell, one side is not flush with the road. A car goes over it and it clunks.
Okay, that's good to know. A cover that's not sitting flush is something we want to look at separately. Is it right in the travel lane, or near the curb where the water is?

Near it. Maybe six, seven feet out from the curb. The water kind of runs toward it, I mean, I don't know if that's connected. Aarav, I said, I'm, ugh, I'm sorry, one second. [pause] Okay. She wants a snack. Go ahead.
You're fine. So what I'll do is open a work order for the drainage at the curb, and note the manhole cover on it too so the crew checks both. Can I get a good callback number?
Got it, 401-555-0188. And your name?
Yusuf Singh. S-I-N-G-H.
So will there be a work order? Like, an actual one, and for what date? Because I need a date. I can't keep walking out there every morning with the kids and hoping nobody breaks a hip.

Yes, there will be an actual work order, I'm entering it right now while we're talking. As for the date, the crews are working through a backlog of drain calls from the snow, so I'd put it in the next few days to a week for someone to get out and look. I'll mark the ice as a safety concern so it gets pushed up.
A week. That's a long time with ice. Can somebody at least put sand or salt down in the meantime? Because it's every night. It freezes, it's black, you can't even see it.

I'll add a request for salt or sand at that spot in the notes. I can't promise it happens the same day, but it'll be on the order so the crew sees it. In the meantime, if you've got any ice melt, a little on the sidewalk side would help.
We have a bag, I guess. I'll do that. It's just, this keeps happening and nobody ever, you know, nobody comes and actually fixes the drain. They look, they go away. And then it's back.
I hear you. I've put in that it's recurring so it doesn't read like a one-off. Whoever's assigned should call you if they need to find the cover or the drain.
Okay. So that's the curb drain, the manhole cover, and the salt. Three things.
That's it exactly. Three things, all at 477 Malbone Road.
Okay. Thank you. I'll, Aarav, that's, honey, that's the wrong, [crosstalk] sorry. Thank you, Denise. Bye.
Take care, Mr. Singh. Bye now.
